meaning: warm and welcoming (to people); enthusiastic; enthusiasm

senses.en: warm, welcoming, friendly in how you treat people (a host, shop staff)
enthusiastic, keen about something
enthusiasm, warmth (工作热情 'enthusiasm for work')

examples.en: People here are all really warm and welcoming.
examples.analysis: 热情 is an adjective here, describing how people treat others: warm, welcoming, keen to help. Like other adjectives it follows 很 directly, with no 是. 都 'all' covers everyone in 这儿的人 'the people here'.

examples.en: The people at that shop aren't very friendly.
examples.analysis: 不太 + 热情 'not very welcoming' is a mild way to complain about service. 家 is the measure word for shops and restaurants (那家店), and 那家店的人 'that shop's people' means the people working there.

examples.en: He's very enthusiastic about his work.
examples.analysis: Here 热情 is a noun, 'enthusiasm', the object of 有: 有热情 'have enthusiasm'. 对 + 工作 names what the enthusiasm is aimed at. 很 can go before 有 + an abstract noun, as in 很有意思.

related.en: friendly (people, relations); calmer than 热情
hot; 热情 is literally 'hot feeling'

meaning: international (mostly right before a noun: 国际机场)

senses.en: international; goes straight before another noun (国际电话 'international call')
the international scene: 在国际上 'internationally, around the world'

examples.en: How do I get to the international airport?
examples.analysis: 国际 goes straight before the noun with no 的: 国际 + 机场. That is how it is mostly used, much like an English adjective. 去 + place + 怎么走 is the standard way to ask for directions.

examples.zh: 我孩子在国际学校上学。
examples.en: My kid goes to an international school.
examples.analysis: 国际学校 'international school': again 国际 sits right before the noun. 在 + place + 上学 = 'go to school at …'. 我孩子 drops 的, which casual speech often does before family words.

examples.en: Are international calls expensive?
examples.analysis: 国际 slips inside the phrase 打电话 'make a phone call': 打 + 国际电话 'make an international call'. 贵不贵 (adjective + 不 + adjective) asks a yes/no question without 吗.

meaning: confidence; faith (in yourself, someone or something)

senses.en: confidence, self-belief: 有信心 'be confident'
faith in someone or something: 对他有信心 'have faith in him'

examples.en: Do you feel confident about the exam?
examples.analysis: 信心 is a noun, so 'be confident' is 有信心 'have confidence'. 考试 is put first as the topic, the thing the confidence is about; then comes a normal 吗 question, 你有信心吗.

examples.en: Don't be scared. I believe in you!
examples.analysis: 对 + person + 有信心 = 'have faith in someone'. 对你 comes before 有信心, not after it as 'in you' does in English. A common line of encouragement before an exam or a big day.

examples.en: He hasn't had much confidence lately.
examples.analysis: 没 + 什么 + noun = 'not much …': 什么 does not ask anything here, it means 'any to speak of'. The sentence is 没(有)信心 with 什么 inserted; 有 is negated with 没, not 不.

related.en: to feel reassured; to stop worrying

meaning: to give (something) to someone as a present

senses.en: to give as a present: 送给 + person (+ thing)
to give away for free: 这些送给你 'you can have these'

examples.zh: 这本书是朋友送给我的。
examples.en: A friend gave me this book.
examples.analysis: 送给 + 我 = 'gave (to) me' as a present. The 是…的 frame picks out one detail of a past event, here who gave it: 是朋友送给我的 'it was a friend who gave it to me'.

examples.zh: 这些衣服我不穿了，送给你吧。
examples.en: I don't wear these clothes anymore. You can have them.
examples.analysis: 送给 + 你 names who gets them; the things given, 这些衣服, sit at the front as the topic. 吧 makes it a casual offer. In 不穿了, 了 marks a change: 'no longer wear'.

examples.zh: 你打算送给他什么礼物？
examples.en: What present are you going to give him?
examples.analysis: 送给 can take two objects: person + thing (他 + 什么礼物). 什么 stands where the answer will go. 送他什么礼物, without 给, means the same and is also very common in speech.

related.en: to give; also to see someone off, to deliver

senses.en: mayor, the head of a city government

measure.note: 一位市长 (polite); 个 in casual talk

examples.en: Who's the new mayor?
examples.analysis: 市长 = 市 'city' + 长 'head', with 长 read zhǎng, not cháng 'long'. The same 长 is in 校长 'principal' and 组长 'team leader'. 新 'new' goes before the noun with no 的.

examples.zh: 我在电视上看到市长了。
examples.en: I saw the mayor on TV.
examples.analysis: 市长 is the object of 看到 'saw'. 在电视上 'on TV' comes before the verb, the usual spot for a phrase saying where an action happens. 了 at the end marks that it happened.

examples.zh: 他爸爸是市长，你不知道吗？
examples.en: His dad is the mayor. Didn't you know?
examples.analysis: 是 + 市长 states someone's position; Chinese needs no word for 'the'. 你不知道吗 'you don't know?' shows surprise, like 'Didn't you know?' in English.

meaning: next; after this; (接下来的) the following

senses.en: next, after this: opens a clause about what comes next
with 的, the next, the following: 接下来的几天 'the next few days'

examples.en: Where are we going next?
examples.analysis: 接下来 'next' opens the sentence and sets the time frame, before the subject 我们, as time words often do. It points to what follows right after the thing you are doing now.

examples.zh: 好，接下来我们看第二个问题。
examples.en: OK, next let's look at the second issue.
examples.analysis: A typical line for running a meeting or a class: 好 closes one part, 接下来 moves on to the next. 第二 + 个 + noun = 'the second …'. 我们看 here works as 'let's look at'.

examples.zh: 接下来的几天都会下雨。
examples.en: It's going to rain every day for the next few days.
examples.analysis: With 的, 接下来 describes a noun: 接下来的几天 'the next few days'. 都 'all' covers each of those days, and 会 predicts what will happen, as in a weather forecast.

related.en: then; links two steps in a sequence

senses.en: credit card

measure.note: 一张信用卡 (张 counts flat things)

examples.en: Can I pay by credit card?
examples.analysis: Chinese says 用信用卡 'use a credit card' for 'pay by card'. 可以…吗 asks for permission. The subject 'I' is left out because the situation at the checkout makes it clear.

examples.zh: 对不起，我们这儿不能用信用卡。
examples.en: Sorry, we don't take credit cards here.
examples.analysis: 不能 + 用信用卡 'can't use a credit card'. 我们这儿 'our place here' means this shop. In China many small shops mainly use mobile payment (WeChat Pay, Alipay) or cash, so this is a line you may well hear.

examples.zh: 我一般用信用卡买东西。
examples.en: I usually pay by credit card when I shop.
examples.analysis: 用信用卡 + 买东西: the first verb phrase gives the means, the second the action, 'use a credit card to buy things'. 一般 'usually' sits right after the subject here; 一般我… at the start is also fine.

collocations.en: to get (apply for) a credit card

senses.en: morning, roughly from dawn to about 8 or 9 a.m.

examples.en: I usually get up at six in the morning.
examples.analysis: 早晨 is a time word, so it goes before the verb, here right after the subject: 我 + 早晨 + 一般 + 六点 + 起床. The bigger unit (morning) comes before the clock time, the reverse of English.

examples.en: The air is lovely in the morning.
examples.analysis: 早晨 + 的 describes a noun: 早晨的空气 'the morning air', the subject of 很好. 早上 means the same and is the more common word in everyday speech.

examples.en: I don't feel like eating in the morning.
examples.analysis: 不想 + verb = 'don't feel like doing'. 早晨 before it sets when this habit applies. 吃东西 'eat things' is the everyday way to say 'eat (anything)'.

related.en: morning; the more common word in speech

senses.en: exit, way out (of a station, building, parking garage)

examples.en: Excuse me, where's the exit?
examples.analysis: 出口 is the subject: thing + 在哪儿 'where is …?'. 请问 'may I ask' is the polite opener with a stranger. 出口 = 出 'go out' + 口 'opening'.

examples.en: I'll wait for you at Exit 2.
examples.analysis: Number + 号 + 出口 names a numbered exit, as in many subway stations: 二号出口 'Exit 2' (二, not 两, because it is a label). 在 + place comes before the verb 等 'wait'.

examples.en: This isn't the exit, it's the entrance.
examples.analysis: 不是 A，是 B corrects a mistake: 'not A, but B'. 出口 'exit' and 入口 'entrance' are the pair you see on signs. The second 是 repeats the verb with the subject left out.

senses.en: the color black; before a noun with 的 (黑色的车) or without it (黑色衣服)

examples.en: Do you have it in black?
examples.analysis: 黑色 + 的 stands for a noun both sides know: 'a black one'. In a shop, 有 + 黑色的 + 吗 asks whether the item comes in black.

examples.zh: 他今天穿了一件黑色的大衣。
examples.en: He wore a black coat today.
examples.analysis: 黑色 describes 大衣 'coat' through 的: number + measure (一件) + 黑色的 + noun. With clothes, 黑色衣服 without 的 is also common.

examples.en: Don't wear black. It's too hot.
examples.analysis: 别 + verb asks someone not to do something. 黑色的 again stands in for the clothes, 'black ones'. 太…了 'too …' gives the reason.

senses.en: to be surnamed: 我姓王 'my surname is Wang'
surname, family name: 这个姓 'this surname'

examples.en: My surname is Wang. My name is Wang Ming.
examples.analysis: 姓 is a verb here: 我 + 姓 + 王 'I am surnamed Wang'. 姓 takes only the surname; 叫 takes the full name (王明) or the given name.

examples.en: What's your teacher's surname?
examples.analysis: 姓 + 什么 asks for a surname; 什么 stands where the answer goes (姓王). To ask the person you are talking to, the polite set phrase is 您贵姓？

examples.en: This surname is very common in China.
examples.analysis: Here 姓 is a noun, 'surname', counted with 个: 这个姓. 在中国 'in China' sits before 很常见 'very common', the normal position for 在 + place when it sets the scene.

related.en: to be called (full or given name)

senses.en: writer, author of literary works: novels, stories, essays, poetry

measure.note: 一位作家 (polite); 个 in casual talk

examples.en: She wants to be a writer.
examples.analysis: 当 + job = 'be, work as': 当作家 'be a writer'. 想 'want to' comes before it. English needs 'a'; Chinese needs no article before 作家.

examples.en: Which writer do you like?
examples.analysis: 哪 + 个 + noun = 'which …?'. The question word stays where the answer goes: 我喜欢 + a name. 作家 means a writer of literary works such as novels, essays or poetry, not just anyone who writes.

examples.zh: 他爸爸是一位有名的作家。
examples.en: His dad is a well-known writer.
examples.analysis: 位 is the polite measure word for people, used here out of respect: 一位 + 有名的 + 作家. 有名 'famous' links to the noun with 的.

related.en: the author of a particular book or article

meaning: level; grade (in a ranked system, e.g. an exam level)

senses.en: level, grade on a scale: number + 级, e.g. 二级 'Level 2', 几级 'what level?'
grade on other scales, e.g. wind force: 五级风 'a force-5 wind'

examples.en: What level have you reached in your Chinese exams?
examples.analysis: Number + 级 names a level, so 几级 asks 'which level?'. 考到 'get to by taking exams' + 了 asks how far you have come so far. 级 takes the number directly, with no measure word.

examples.en: I passed Level 2 last year.
examples.analysis: 二级 'Level 2' uses 二, not 两: it names a level rather than counting two of them. 考过 here means 'pass (an exam)', with 过 (guò) showing the result of 考.

examples.en: My Chinese isn't at Level 3 yet.
examples.analysis: 不到 + 三级 'not up to Level 3'. 还 'still' suggests the speaker expects to get there. Number + 级 works like a noun here, the object of 到 'reach'.

related.en: year or grade at school (三年级 'third grade')

senses.en: a long time: before 没/不 + verb, 'not … for ages' (好久没见)
after a verb, how long something went on: 等了好久 'waited ages'

examples.en: Long time no see! How have you been?
examples.analysis: 好久 'a long time' comes before 不见 'not see': 好久不见 is the set greeting for someone you haven't seen in a while. 最近怎么样 'how have things been lately?' often follows.

examples.en: I've been waiting ages for you!
examples.analysis: After a verb and its object, 好久 says how long the action has gone on: 等你 + 好久. 了 at the end counts that time up to now. Said to someone who turns up late.

examples.en: I haven't had dumplings in ages.
examples.analysis: Before 没 + verb, 好久 says how long something has not happened: 好久 + 没吃 + 饺子. 了 at the end marks this as the situation now. Compare 等你好久了, where the time follows the verb.

related.en: (casual) a long while; also half a day

meaning: customer (of a shop, restaurant or service)

senses.en: customer, shopper; someone a shop or restaurant serves

measure.note: 一位顾客 (polite); 个 in casual talk

examples.en: There are really a lot of customers today.
examples.analysis: Quantity is the predicate here: 顾客 + 特别多 'customers are especially many'. Noun + 多 is a common way to say 'there are a lot of …'. 今天 sets the time at the front.

examples.zh: 我们店的老顾客都很喜欢这个菜。
examples.en: Our regular customers all love this dish.
examples.analysis: 老 + 顾客 = 'regular customer': here 老 means 'long-standing', not 'old in age'. 我们店的老顾客 is the whole subject, and 都 sums them up before 很喜欢. 顾客 is the standard word for a shop's or restaurant's customers; it sounds a little businesslike, and in everyday speech staff also say 客人.

examples.en: There's a customer here to see you.
examples.analysis: 有 + 位 + 顾客 + 找你: 有 brings in someone new, then a verb says what they do. 有位 is short for 有一位; 一 is often dropped in casual speech. 位 is the polite measure word for people.

related.en: guest; also used for customers in shops and restaurants

meaning: convenient; handy; (of time) a good time for someone

senses.en: convenient, handy: easy to reach or to use (交通很方便)
suitable, OK for someone right now: 你方便吗？ 'is this a good time?'

examples.en: Getting around here is really easy.
examples.analysis: 方便 'convenient' is the adjective predicate after 很: 交通 + 很方便 'transport is convenient'. Said about where you live or work, meaning buses and the subway are close and easy to use.

examples.en: Is now a good time to talk?
examples.analysis: Here 方便 means 'suitable for you right now': 说话方便吗 'is talking convenient (for you)?'. A polite way to open a phone call before getting to the point.

examples.zh: 明天不太方便，后天行吗？
examples.en: Tomorrow isn't great for me. Would the day after tomorrow work?
examples.analysis: 不太方便 'not very convenient' is a polite way to turn down a time without giving a reason. 后天行吗 'is the day after tomorrow OK?' then offers another day.

collocations.en: easy to get around; good transport

senses.en: yellow: as a predicate (太黄了), before a noun (黄头发) or with 的 (黄的); 黄色 is the color name
(of eyes, skin, paper) yellowish, gone yellow

examples.en: Do you want the yellow one or the red one?
examples.analysis: 黄 + 的 = 'a yellow one'; the noun drops out because both sides can see it. A 还是 B asks 'A or B?'. 黄 also works alone as a predicate (太黄了) or right before a noun (黄头发); the color name is 黄色.

examples.zh: 他眼睛有点儿黄，得去看病。
examples.en: His eyes look a bit yellow. He needs to see a doctor.
examples.analysis: 黄 is the adjective predicate after 有点儿 'a bit', which usually signals something unwelcome. 得 (read děi here) means 'have to': 得去看病 'needs to go and see a doctor'.

examples.zh: 这个灯太黄了，换个白的吧。
examples.en: This light is too yellow. Let's get a white one.
examples.analysis: 太 + 黄 + 了 = 'too yellow', a complaint. In 换个白的 'change to a white one', 个 is short for 一个 and 白的 means 'a white one'. 吧 makes it a suggestion.

related.en: yellow, the color as a noun; careful: before 电影/小说/网站 it means 'pornographic'
Mr. Huang (黄 is also a common surname)

senses.en: point of view, standpoint on a question; more formal than 看法

examples.zh: 这个问题你有什么观点？
examples.en: What's your view on this question?
examples.analysis: 你有什么观点 'what view do you have?' is a standard way to ask for someone's opinion. The topic, 这个问题, comes first. 观点 sounds a little formal, suited to meetings and discussions; in casual chat people say 你怎么看？

examples.zh: 我明白你的观点，但是我不这么想。
examples.en: I see your point, but I don't see it that way.
examples.analysis: 明白 + 你的观点 'understand your point of view' acknowledges the other side before 但是 'but'. 不这么想 'don't think this way' keeps the disagreement polite.

examples.en: People's views aren't quite the same.
examples.analysis: 观点 is the subject: 大家的观点 'everyone's views'. 不太一样 'not quite the same' is a gentle way to say people disagree. With no plural ending, 观点 covers one view or many.

related.en: opinion; also an objection or complaint

senses.en: novel, a book-length story: 一本小说 'a novel'
fiction, stories in general: 看小说 'read fiction'

measure.note: 一本小说 (a book); 部 counts it as a work

examples.en: Do you like reading novels?
examples.analysis: Chinese usually says 看小说 'look at novels' for reading them; 读小说 is also correct but sounds more bookish. 喜欢 + verb phrase = 'like doing'. With no measure word, 小说 means novels in general.

examples.zh: 这本小说很长，我看了一半。
examples.en: This novel is long. I'm halfway through.
examples.analysis: 本 is the measure word for books: 这本小说 'this novel'. In 看了一半 'have read half', 了 marks the part done so far and 一半 'half' says how much.

examples.en: He's been writing fiction online lately.
examples.analysis: 写小说 'write fiction'. 在网上 'online' comes before the verb as a place phrase. Online serial novels are hugely popular in China, so this is a common hobby or side job.

senses.en: snow; 'to snow' is 下雪, literally 'snow falls'

examples.en: It's really snowing hard!
examples.analysis: 雪 is the subject and 下 'fall' the verb: snow 'falls' in Chinese, as rain does (下雨). 得 + 真大 describes how it is falling: 'really heavily'.

examples.en: Have you ever seen snow?
examples.analysis: 雪 is the object of 见过 'have seen (at some point)': 过 marks experience, 'ever, at some point'. A natural question for someone from a warm country.

examples.en: There's no snow here in winter.
examples.analysis: 没有 + 雪 'there is no snow': 没有 denies that something exists. The place 这儿 and the time 冬天 both come before it. 'To snow' would be 下雪, so 'it doesn't snow here' is 这儿不下雪.
